name: Waldorf Astoria Shanghai on the Bund
positioning: Heritage hotel in the restored 1911 Shanghai Club building, one block from the Bund with Huangpu River views
best_for: Travelers who want a historic base by the Bund
Guests who love afternoon tea and cocktail bars

facts.text: The Heritage Building is a landmark built in 1911 that was once the Shanghai Club.
The heritage building was restored using archival photographs and historical records.
The hotel is one block from the Bund and has views of the Huangpu River.
Wai King Kok, on the fifth floor of the Waldorf Astoria Club, serves Cantonese and Chinese cuisine.
Ling Long serves modern Chinese cuisine by Chef Jason.
Grand Brasserie recreates a classic European brasserie and overlooks an interior courtyard garden.
Peacock Alley serves afternoon tea and light dining and is inspired by Waldorf Astoria New York.
The Waldorf Spa combines traditional Chinese practices with modern techniques.
The hotel has an indoor pool and a fitness center.
Rooms and suites have fine linens and a marble bathroom.

highlights.text: The Long Bar has been restored to its original Shanghai Club grandeur.
Pink Oyster, at the Long Bar, is an intimate eight-seat oyster omakase serving a ten-course degustation.
It was the first Waldorf Astoria hotel to open in Asia.
Salon de Ville serves a Red Velvet Afternoon Tea with views across Pudong and the Bund.
Suites in the old building, now called the Waldorf Astoria Club, have colonial-style touches such as poster beds, walk-in closets and claw-foot tubs.

considerations.text: To reserve at Ling Long, guests are asked to call the restaurant directly.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing and that the historic building's layout may feel formal for some guests.
